messages.subject: mirt model for exploratory purpose
parts:
Hi Phil

I'm constructing a new meausrment instrument for asseassing risk management quality within companies and I'm using mirt package to run an exploratory mirt model to determin the number of dimensions or latent traits in the instrument but i can't find a procedure to do that. I know that for classical factor analysis the number of factors correspond to the eignvalues greater than 1, but I don't know if it exists a similiar procedure to do that in mirt.

the problem is that the measure is newly developed and ther's no theoritical foundation for the number of factors to adopt, so I relally need this exploratory analysis.*

any help concerning this issue will be really appreciated. 

Thank you phill for your kind support.

messages.author: 70d0917afd869432
messages.subject: Re: mirt model for exploratory purpose
parts:
The basic mirt model is exploratory (with model being a scalar input).  Simply run mirt(dat, model = 1) to get the unidimensional model, mirt(dat, 2) for a 2 factor, and so on.  Make sure to use the proper item type. For determining which is better, look at the fit statistics across models, compare them with anova(), etc.

Hope that helps!
